claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 went live at 22:00 the prior night: multi-node orders now reserve stock from the east node first. Change review passed and regression suite was green.
claims.corroboration: Single tier-1 verified source owned by Inventory Control (rule owner); sufficient for established per rules.
claims.limitation: Passing review/regression does not rule out an unanticipated interaction with multi-node split-reservation logic.

claims.statement: From 06:00, orders held in 'allocated, awaiting pickup' for more than 90 minutes reached 9% of overnight allocations, entirely on east-node lanes; other nodes are normal.
claims.corroboration: Tier-1 verified monitor alert from observability.
claims.limitation: The alert itself states it cannot attribute a cause; east-node-only pattern is temporally correlated with C1 but not yet causally established.

claims.statement: Every held order was routed to the east node and flagged by the overnight allocator as a split-reservation exception; reports began about 06:00 and are ongoing.
claims.corroboration: Single tier-2 customer_support source; non-authoritative per its own flag.
claims.limitation: Not yet corroborated by an authoritative allocation-system source (Inventory Control owns allocation exceptions); cannot be established or used as root_cause discriminating evidence until audited directly.

claims.statement: Inventory Control reported (07:20) that allocation totals reconcile and nothing looks wrong on their side.
claims.limitation: Informal chat statement, not a system audit; tentatively weighs against inventory_count_drift as the mechanism but is not confirmatory.

claims.statement: Carrier ops on-call (07:31) found nothing obvious in the dock schedule.
claims.corroboration: Single tier-2 incident_chat source, non-authoritative, preliminary look only.
claims.limitation: Preliminary/informal; does not rule out dock_capacity or carrier_feed_lag causes, just no obvious finding yet.

claims.statement: Dashboards only count orders by state; they cannot show how a booked pickup relates to the carrier's own confirmation, and Inventory Control has no visibility into carrier-side records.
claims.limitation: This is a structural observability gap affecting the investigation, not evidence of root cause itself.

next_action.rationale: C3 (split-reservation exceptions on held orders) rests on a single non-authoritative support_report source and is the only lead directly tying the 06:00 stuck cohort to the v18 rule change (C1). Auditing allocation exceptions directly from the authoritative allocation system (owned by Inventory Control) can corroborate or refute C3 from a distinct, higher-trust owner, and can reveal whether the exceptions are specifically caused by the east-node-first reservation logic in v18 versus some other mechanism (carrier feed lag, dock capacity, inventory drift).
next_action.expected_information_gain: Either establishes C3 with a second distinct-owner source (moving toward established/root_cause-eligible with discriminating evidence linking v18 to the stuck orders), or refutes/narrows it, ruling allocation_rule_defect in or out before considering carrier- or dock-side diagnostics.
